claims.text: Controlled post-deformation annealing will improve ductility in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Controlled post-deformation annealing will promote more uniform deformation in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed annealing treatment will not significantly reduce strength.
The proposed annealing treatment will not significantly reduce impact-induced energy release.
Conventionally cast and solutionized refractory HEAs have moderate dendritic segregation and residual stresses.
Dendritic segregation and residual stresses limit ductility in the proposed baseline material.
The untreated material has high strength and strong impact-induced energy release but undergoes localized deformation.
Annealing at approximately 1000°C for 1 hour in argon will promote partial recrystallization.
Annealing at approximately 1000°C for 1 hour in argon will relax grain-boundary stresses.
Partial recrystallization and stress relaxation will produce refined, equiaxed grains and a more uniform residual-stress distribution.
The annealed microstructure will retain a sufficiently high dislocation density to preserve strength.
Thermally activated recovery, grain-boundary relaxation, and formation of small new grains will distribute strain more uniformly.
Retained dislocation structures will preserve both strength and the energetic characteristics of the alloy.
The proposed balance of recrystallization and retained dislocations will avoid the usual ductility-strength trade-off in refractory materials.
The effective annealing window is expected to be approximately 900–1100°C for durations up to 1 hour.
Annealing well above 1100°C or substantially longer than 1 hour could cause over-recrystallization, grain coarsening, strength loss, or degradation of energetic response.
Processing in a non-inert atmosphere could cause oxidation and formation of undesired secondary phases.
Thermally induced grain refinement is well established in many alloys.
Recrystallization kinetics and length scales in multicomponent refractory HEAs are uncertain and may depend on minor compositional variations.
